Business goal: Show which eligible capabilities are already assigned to a tenant-local role and which are not.
User outcome: Root user can compare assigned vs unassigned capabilities for one tenant role before making edits.
Notes / constraints: Must stay tenant-scoped and must not confuse platform template defaults with current tenant-local assignments; protected mandatory grants should be identifiable.

Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-side visibility; future root-admin UI only.
Backend enforcement rule: Root-user-only management route plus central authorization seam; compares assigned tenant grants against eligible capability catalog.
Session / expiry behavior: Requires valid root-user session; acts on one target tenant context.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side tenant behavior in phase one.
Request contract: params { tenantId, roleKey }, query { assignmentState?, search? }
Response contract: 200 list of eligible capability descriptors with assignmentState=assigned|unassigned and mandatory/protected markers
Cross-feature seams: Depends on rootAuth authenticated root-user session context and tenant existence seam; consumes global capability catalog metadata.
Persistence impact: Read tenant role capability grants against eligible capability catalog.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique tenant-role/capability grant mapping; indexes on (tenantId, roleKey) and capabilityKey.
Search / filter model: Exact tenant-role lookup with assignment-state filter and capability search.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam plus root-user-only backend guard
Audit requirement: Privileged inspection of tenant-role assignments should be audit-visible where admin-read audit policy requires.
Privacy / personal data impact: Processes tenant identifiers and operator-authored metadata.
Standards impact: Touches tenant isolation, least privilege, protected capability governance, and admin control review.

Audit tests: Verify privileged admin-read audit behavior if required by policy.
